title: West Fertilizer: ammonium-nitrate inventory, responder exposure, and land-use/regulatory gaps
summary: West Fertilizer is encoded as a high-sensitivity process-safety and offsite-consequence record: fertilizer-grade ammonium-nitrate storage, fire/explosion hazard awareness, emergency-response preparation, land-use proximity, and regulatory coverage are the first-pass grain.

status_history.note: Added as process-safety / CSB lane record.

subjects.name: U.S. Chemical Safety and Hazard Investigation Board
West Volunteer Fire Department and surrounding community

claims.claim: The CSB investigation page records the West Fertilizer incident as an April 17, 2013 chemical distribution fire and explosion in West, Texas, and states that the massive explosion fatally injured twelve volunteer firefighters and two members of the public and caused hundreds of injuries.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: The CSB final report cover identifies the case as West Fertilizer Company Fire and Explosion, states 15 fatalities and more than 260 injured, and lists key issues: regulatory oversight, hazard awareness, emergency planning and response, fertilizer-grade ammonium-nitrate storage practices, and land-use planning/zoning.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: The final report table of contents exposes the intended evidentiary grain: FGAN properties and hazards, factors contributing to massive fire/explosion, emergency response, limited/conflicting guidance, lessons not learned, safety management programs, EPA RMP, emergency planning, fire-protection codes, and land use.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: The West record is encoded as an inventory, siting, hazard-awareness, emergency-planning, and regulatory-coverage case; it is not merely an ignition-origin story and not merely a firefighter-response story.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: The case is especially important for the cube because a small community, responder knowledge, facility inventory, material storage, regulatory gaps, and land-use proximity become a single coupled consequence surface.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

type_payload.system: fertilizer-grade ammonium nitrate storage/distribution facility, emergency response system, land-use and regulatory environment

sequence_of_events.event: Fire developed at facility storing FGAN.
Responders and public were exposed to escalating fire/explosion conditions.
FGAN detonation caused catastrophic community damage and fatalities.
CSB traced the case through storage, awareness, emergency planning, regulatory oversight, and land-use surfaces.

type_payload.proximate_cause: FGAN fire/explosion sequence; exact ignition-origin details are not the promoted grain in this one-pass record.
contributing_factors: emergency planning and responder information gaps
latent_conditions: low-frequency catastrophic hazard treated as ordinary local inventory
community and responder exposure not fully converted into enforceable controls
fragmented authority across fire, fertilizer, environmental, labor, and land-use regimes

handling_notes: Preserve worker/community dignity and avoid casualty spectacle.
Use investigation language to understand system conditions, not to assign unsourced individual blame.
Record source boundaries and avoid regulatory/political overreach.
